ei.title: The Science Behind the Mona Lisa
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
The Science Behind the Mona Lisa

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.

questions.passage: The Science Behind the Mona Lisa Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most (A)[intelligent / ordinary] painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an (B)[accomplished / amateur] scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually (C)[exclusive / inclusive]. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 가장 지적인(intelligent) 화가 중 한 명이며, 뛰어난(accomplished) 과학자이기도 했고, 예술과 과학은 상호 배타적(exclusive)이지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② intelligent — accomplished — exclusive: 원문 일치
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): 지적인이 맞음
❌ ④ amateur(아마추어): 뛰어난이 맞음

questions.passage: In fact, it was largely through a (A)[scientific / artistic] approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was (B)[fascinated / repelled] by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in (C)[anatomy / geometry] allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 과학적(scientific) 접근으로 걸작을 창조했고, 미소에 매료(fascinated)되어 해부학(anatomy)에 관심을 가졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ scientific — fascinated — anatomy: 원문 일치
❌ ① repelled(혐오된): 매료된이 맞음
❌ ② artistic(예술적): 과학적 접근
❌ ③ geometry(기하학): 해부학이 맞음

questions.passage: He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the (A)[perception / deception] that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the (B)[illusion / reality] of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more (C)[subtle / vivid] the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 눈이 우리를 본다는 인식(perception), 깊이의 착각(illusion), 더 미묘한(subtle) 색상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① perception — illusion — subtle: 원문 일치
❌ ② reality(현실): 착각이 맞음
❌ ③ deception(속임): 인식이 맞음
❌ ④ vivid(선명한): 미묘한이 맞음
det.tip: perception(인식) ↔ deception(속임). illusion(착각) ↔ reality(현실). subtle(미묘한) ↔ vivid(선명한).

questions.passage:
The Science Behind the Mona Lisa

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most ①<u>intelligent</u> painters in the history of art.  Although he is best known for his artistic ②<u>masterpieces</u>, he was also an accomplished scientist.  During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually ③<u>inclusive</u>.  Rather, one was seen as ④<u>informing</u> upon the other.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ inclusive(포괄적인) → exclusive(배타적인): 예술과 과학이 상호 배타적이지 않았다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① intelligent: 원문 일치
✅ ② masterpieces: 원문 일치
❌ ③ inclusive → exclusive: mutually exclusive
✅ ④ informing: 원문 일치
det.tip: exclusive(배타적인) ↔ inclusive(포괄적인). mutually exclusive = 상호 배타적.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① bored(지루해하는) → fascinated(매료된): 미소 형성에 매료되었다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① bored → fascinated: 매료됨
✅ ② evaluated: 원문 일치
✅ ③ determine: 원문 일치
✅ ④ mysterious: 원문 일치

questions.passage: He also carefully ①<u>positioned</u> the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is ②<u>slightly</u> turned, while the eyes still face the viewer.  Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are ③<u>staring</u> straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting.  Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of ④<u>flatness</u> in the painting.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ flatness(평면감) → depth(깊이감): 그림에 깊이의 착각을 만들었다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① positioned: 원문 일치
✅ ② slightly: 원문 일치
✅ ③ staring: 원문 일치
❌ ④ flatness → depth: 깊이의 착각

questions.passage:

❌ ② amateur(아마추어): 반의어

det.korean: magnificent = 훌륭한, 장엄한
det.analysis:
✅ ② splendid(훌륭한): 동의어
❌ ① mediocre(보통의): 반의어
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): 반의어

det.korean: determine = 결정하다, 확인하다
det.analysis:
✅ ④ identify(확인하다): 동의어
❌ ① ignore(무시하다): 반의어
❌ ② delay(지연하다): 관련 없음
❌ ③ assume(가정하다): 관련 없음

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form.  So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle.  This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's <u>mysterious</u> smile.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 mysterious와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: mysterious = 신비로운. 반의어 = obvious(명백한).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ obvious(명백한): 반의어
❌ ① enigmatic(수수께끼 같은): 동의어
❌ ② puzzling(당혹스러운): 유사어
❌ ④ complex(복잡한): 관련 없음

questions.passage: Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting.  The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more <u>subtle</u> the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 subtle와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: subtle = 미묘한, 은은한. 반의어 = bold(대담한, 두드러진).
det.analysis:
✅ ② bold(대담한): 반의어
❌ ① gentle(부드러운): 유사어
❌ ③ faint(희미한): 유사어
❌ ④ soft(부드러운): 유사어

questions.stem: 다음 두 문장의 밑줄 친 face의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) face = 얼굴(명사). (B) face = 향하다(동사).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) 얼굴 — (B) 향하다
❌ ① 둘 다 얼굴: (B)는 동사

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "something that appears to exist or be true but does not actually exist or is not actually true"

det.korean: 존재하거나 사실인 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 아닌 것 = illusion(착각, 환각)
det.analysis:
✅ ① illusion(착각): 정의 일치
❌ ② perception(인식): 실제 감각
❌ ③ reality(현실): 반대
❌ ④ depth(깊이): 관련 없음
det.tip: illusion = 착각, 환상. the illusion of depth.
